Definition: from G5507 and G757; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel:--(chief, high) captain.
BiblicalUsage: Chiliarchos is the commander of a thousand, the chief captain, and the New Testament uses it for the officers who carry out orders. The chief captain at Jerusalem takes Paul with soldiers and chains, the captain with his officers takes Jesus in the garden, Herod's chief captains sit at his birthday feast, and the captains of the earth hide themselves in the day of wrath.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word shows how earthly power works: it takes orders and it takes prisoners, but it cannot hold the One it arrests. I hold that every captain in these passages is small beside the King they stand against.
